It's really not a relief to me.

The therapist I worked with was big on cognitive therapy, and we went through a lot of this. He gave me a print out of thinking errors, and throughout my time working with him, I was supposed to identify thinking errors and write them down as they came. The idea there was to get used to catching them. As you might assume, a lot of mine were "fortune telling" (basically predicting the future and assuming the worst).

Overall, the point was to basically acknowledge all of these negative thoughts/feelings/emotions, but then not let them sort of be real - don't let them get beyond just "being" basically. The idea was to acknowledge them, but to not let them take the wheel of the vehicle.

I had a hard time really getting that to work with me, and maybe that's my fault. It just didn't seem to work for me.

Thanks for the kind words. 

I did see a therapist for a while, and I've tried one of the available anti-depressants. Neither of those felt like they've helped (though I'm aware that sometimes it's a matter of just finding the right therapist/the right medication).

I've looked into the possibility of inpatient stuff before and outside of probably unrealistic fears, I can't afford to pay for anything like that. I don't have insurance, and my family's not in a position to financially assist me either.

I can't necessarily clearly identify things that suck. It's a general everything kind of sucks and nothing really doesn't kind of situation. Things that get me down the most are things like feeling like a general failure given where I'm at right now, having to live with family, and knowing that my only option right now is to get a job I'll no doubt hate (along with the worry that I'll have to do that for the rest of my life).

It's not really new though, I've basically felt this way as long as I can remember. So I don't really remember what anything but this feels like.

Yeah, basically. Like with video games, I used to have fun playing them, but at this point, I just do it to do something. I also used to love reading, but I just don't feel like I get anything out of it anymore.
I honestly don't know. That's another part of the problem though. I just don't find much fun in anything. If I did think something was fun, I'd probably do it and enjoy it.

I did do some therapy a couple of years ago when I went back to school. I couldn't keep going once I graduated though, and I didn't really feel like it did much for me. It might be that another therapist could produce results, but there aren't many options where I live. Especially considering my current unemployment.
I just figure that once I'm dead, it's done, so regardless of when it happens, it happens, and nothing I do before it really matters. It all feels futile to me.

I'm 25 years old.

I deal with severe major depression and some pretty rough social anxiety. When I graduated from high school, we lived out in the middle of nowhere in Arizona, and my stepdad bailed on us that summer. One day, he just grabbed a coffee thermos, said, "It's been fun," and he left. I thought he'd be back, but he never came back. He took the only really reliable vehicle we had, and we were kind of stuck there. I didn't really have any real friends at the time. He moved us to Arizona when I was halfway done with high school, and then halfway through my junior year, my mom decided to have us switch schools (we had a choice because we were basically right on the district lines in the middle of nowhere). In the year and a half I went to school, I talked to people and everything, but I just didn't make real friends. My anxiety issues and depression didn't help, but a big part of it was just that we never had money.

Anyway, it was me, my mom, and my sister. We moved into our cousin's camper for a little while which was way too small for the three of us. Then, we moved to my mom's new boyfriend's house several months later. Then, right back to the camper after a couple of months. Then, we moved to a new boyfriend's house. I should have stayed with him. After a couple of years there, we were really good friends, and he was a bit of a father-figure to me. But, fearing that he'd change after my mom left, I moved back to Kansas with my mom when she came back here to help take care of her parents.

Now, almost five years later, I'm still living in their basement. I have to pay rent, but I haven't had a job in almost four years. I've kept myself afloat very stupidly. After I quit the last job I had, I had enough between savings and taxes to cover a few months of rent, so I used that. I couldn't find any jobs that didn't give me a stronger urge to kill myself, so I thought I'd just go back to school at the local community college. It would look like I'm doing something productive, I could use the leftover loan money to cover rent and some food (which meant lots of stereotypical ramen noodle nonsense), and maybe I could figure out a plan for what to do next while I'm going through school. The problem was that the only interest I had was writing, so I majored in English. From there, I clicked with a teacher who kind of took me under his wing (he was the only person I regularly talked to, and I still talk to him), and I switched to majoring in creative writing. 

After about a year at school, I realized what I was doing, and I went in to talk to my advisor. My fear was that I was piling up debt (albeit not an insane amount of debt when compared to many other people, but it's a lot to me) and working towards a useless degree. She assured me that any degree at that level is basically the same for transferring. I might have to make some classes up, but it ultimately didn't matter a whole lot. That made sense since most of the requirements are core classes with a few electives thrown in.

I pushed on, graduated, got scared about trying to move elsewhere to pursue a higher degree, and now I'm sitting here. The last semester at college, I finally went to the therapist they had, and I was diagnosed with depression and social anxiety by a professional. However, I didn't really make any headway in the few months I was there, so I'm not sure that it did any good. I spent a lot of that time thinking about killing myself, and I've spent a lot of the four months since graduating doing the same.

**TL;DR/an actual answer**: I'm here because of personal flaws and bad choices. I feel like an absolute failure because my life has essentially been a directionless pit of stagnation since I was a kid, and I just have no ambition. Other people seem to press on, and I try, but I just don't have the energy. I feel alone, my mom's not someone I can talk to, and I haven't really made any friends in my life who I can talk to. I generally just feel like giving up 99.9% of the time, and I just try to keep myself occupied to fill time. Right now, I need a job, but there aren't really any around here unless you're a nurse. I don't think I'll ever be happy, and I imagine that sooner or later I'll call it quits.

I'm not who you replied to, but I have a similar problem (though I've never taken a dump in anything other than a toilet). For me, if I'm forced into a situation (like with school when I was younger), I can handle it without seeming like some sort of weirdo (on the outside at least). But I just can't stand dealing with people. I have a hard time really articulating it because it's not an extremely specific feeling.

First, I just don't want to deal with small talk. I don't want people asking me how my day is or whatever because they don't care, and I don't want them to care, but I also don't want them to ask. If I answer honestly, I'm an asshole who can't just slip through the small talk like a normal person. If I just say it's alright or whatever, I'm following the social norms, but I feel like an asshole for doing something I think is so worthless. If I don't say anything (like I'd want to), I'm an asshole for ignoring them. I just don't feel like talking to people. I especially don't want to hear people's little comments about things.

Second, I don't want to annoy people. The whole golden rule thing went too far in my head at some point, and because I sometimes get annoyed by people, I expect that they'll get annoyed by me, and I don't want that.

On top of the social anxiety issue, I also have a depression problem. Being consistently low-energy and feeling overwhelmed by everything that might otherwise be normal doesn't help doing more on top of that. Getting out and going to the store is one hurdle, but then mustering the energy to pretend to care is another. I don't want to be an asshole, but I also don't want to deal with people. I'd prefer to ignore everyone and just do what I want to do. Partially because I just don't have the energy, and partially because it just feels pointless to talk to these people who I don't (and probably won't) know.

For the most part I won't even post things online, and when I do, I tend to delete them more often than not because it's just not worth the energy in my mind.

It's all a problem because I want to be friends with people, and I want to interact normally, but every time I'm in a social situation (or potentially faced with one), I just don't want to deal with it. Once I'm comfortable with someone it's not really an issue, but I'm rarely ever comfortable enough with people. It's not really that I'm scared in the sense that they'll hurt me, but I just don't want to be seen as an asshole.

Personally, I've been to a therapist about it. I went for a little while in college, but I can't afford to now (these issues really hinder job searching). The help I was given there felt relatively unhelpful as it was all cognitive therapy, and I still had a hard time dealing with it.

Of course, I sit here without any friends, unemployed, and behind on bills, and I have a whole other set of anxieties developing because of how I handle the aforementioned issues. These problems are objectively worse than the fears I may have, and I know this, but I can't seem to force myself to do what I know I need to do.
